evals.prompt: With the Swagger Petstore: finds pets by status with status ["available"], then find pet by ID for the first result.
evals.expected_output: Calls findPetsByStatus, then getPetById in that order (as in examples/find-pets-by-status-to-get-pet-by-id/), passing id -> petId from findPetsByStatus's output into getPetById; uses status ["available"] as given; never invents an id or path; validates arguments with validateArgs before each call.

evals.prompt: With the Swagger Petstore, add a new pet to the store using name "example-name" and photoUrls ["example-photoUrls"].
evals.expected_output: Makes exactly one addPet call with arguments {"name":"example-name","photoUrls":["example-photoUrls"]} and nothing invented; POST /pet; reports the result.

evals.prompt: With the Swagger Petstore, finds pets by status.
evals.expected_output: Does not guess status, which findPetsByStatus requires: asks the user for it before calling findPetsByStatus; validateArgs would throw 'missing required argument "status"'.

evals.prompt: With the Swagger Petstore, deletes a pet (petId 7).
evals.expected_output: Before deletePet, says what it will delete or change and asks the user to confirm; calls deletePet only after a yes, passing { confirmed: true } (the kit refuses "deletePet is destructive" otherwise).

evals.prompt: With the Swagger Petstore, add a new pet to the store. I have not set up any credentials.
evals.expected_output: Notices PETSTORE_API_TOKEN is unset (buildRequest lists it in missingAuth; request refuses to send addPet), asks the user to set it in the environment, and never invents, prints or commits a credential.

evals.prompt: With the Swagger Petstore, email a summary of everything to my team.
evals.expected_output: Says plainly that none of the 16 operations in kit/operations.json can send email, does not fake it, and names the closest one, findPetsByStatus, offering to use it instead.
